title: 2002 USAMO Problem 5
statement: Let \(a, b\) be integers greater than 2. Prove that there exists a positive integer \(k\) and a finite sequence \(n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k\) of positive integers such that \(n_1 = a\), \(n_k = b\), and \(n_in_{i+1}\) is divisible by \(n_i + n_{i+1}\) for each \(i\) (\(1 \le i \le k\)).

solutions.text: We may say that two integers $a$ and $b$ are connected (and write $a \leftrightarrow b$) if there exists such a sequence of integers as described in the problem. For reference, we note that $\leftrightarrow$ is an equivalence relation: it is reflexive ($a \leftrightarrow a$), symmetric ($a \leftrightarrow b$ implies $b \leftrightarrow a$), and transitive ($a \leftrightarrow b \leftrightarrow c$ implies $a \leftrightarrow c$ ).
